subject: A question on Rasch Vs. 2PL with same a

messages.author: 0fae840788d5acb9
messages.subject: A question on Rasch Vs. 2PL with same a
parts:
Hi Phil,

 

I have a question on the difference between Rasch/PCM and 2PL/GPCM that have equal slope parameters. On page 107 of your latest mirt package document, in the explanation of argument itemtype, you wrote “'Rasch' - Rasch/partial credit model by constraining slopes to 1 and freely estimating the variance parameters (alternatively, can be specified by applying equality constraints to the slope parameters in 'gpcm'; Rasch, 1960)”. I don’t think these two models are the same, as the 2PL/GPCM estimates one more parameter, a1, in addition to the ones estimated by Rasch/PCM.

Moreover, the anova result of the Rasch/PCM and 2PL/GPCM is really weird: the df is 0 instead of 1.

 

For better explanation, please try the following code:

data <- expand.table(LSAT7)[1:500,]

mod_rasch <- mirt(data, itemtype = "Rasch")

mod_equala <- mirt(data, itemtype = "2PL", constrain = list(seq(1, by=4, length.out=ncol(data))))

anova(mod_rasch, mod_equala)

 

Waiting for your reply. Thanks again for developing the mirt R package.
